[[9 ABY]] {{C|Epilogue}} }} {{Quote|''Star Wars Rebels'' is an adventure show that focuses on a street-smart teenage boy who just might have what it takes to be a Jedi, and who joins a small band of rebels that engages in daring missions of resistance against the evil Galactic Empire.|[[Rayne Roberts]], [[Star Wars Insider 152|''Star Wars Insider'' 152]]|{{InsiderCite|152|Rebel Friends!}}}} '''''Star Wars Rebels''''' is an animated television series set during the [[time]] frame between the films [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'']] and [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']]. It premiered worldwide as a one-hour television movie, ''[[Star Wars Rebels: Spark of Rebellion]]'', on [[Disney Channel]] on [[October 3]], [[2014]]; Regular episodes aired for four seasons on [[Disney XD]], from [[October 13]], 2014 to [[March 5]], [[2018]]. During its run, the series was nominated for four [[Wikipedia:Emmy Awards|Emmy Awards]], including two consecutive nominations for "Outstanding Children's Program."{{WebCite|url=https://www.emmys.com/shows/star-wars-rebels|text=Star Wars Rebels AWARDS & NOMINATIONS|work=[https://www.emmys.com emmys.com]|archivedate=20190904082728}} The series follows a motley group of [[Spectres|rebels]] who live aboard the [[VCX-100 light freighter|starship]] ''[[Ghost]]'' as they [[Early rebellion against the Galactic Empire|fight]] the [[Galactic Empire]]. The rebels include [[Ezra Bridger]], a young orphan from [[Lothal]] who learns he can use [[the Force]]; [[Kanan Jarrus]], a [[Jedi]] who survived [[Order 66]]; [[Hera Syndulla]], a [[Twi'lek]] [[pilot]] and veteran resistance fighter; [[Sabine Wren]], a [[Mandalore|Mandalorian]] explosives expert; [[Garazeb Orrelios|Garazeb "Zeb" Orrelios]], a [[Lasat]] warrior; and the cantankerous [[astromech droid]] [[C1-10P]], also known as Chopper. The crew will eventually help give rise to the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic|Rebel Alliance]]. Lucasfilm first announced ''Star Wars Rebels'' on [[May 20]], [[2013]], following the news that the animated television series ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'' would be ending and that a new series would be produced. ''Star Wars Rebels'' was the first new major ''Star Wars'' project to be released following [[The Walt Disney Company]]'s acquisition of [[Lucasfilm]] in [[2012]]. The series was created by [[Dave Filoni]], [[Simon Kinberg]], and [[Carrie Beck]], and stars actors [[Taylor Gray]], [[Freddie Prinze Jr.]], [[Vanessa Marshall]], [[Tiya Sircar]], [[Steve Blum]], and Dave Filoni. ==Plot summary== ===Premise=== {{Quote|…we're going to really show the origins of the rebellion. When our series begins, it's not the Rebel Alliance yet; we start with a group of rebels. It'll be really interesting to show the progress of the Alliance forming…|Executive producer Greg Weisman, ''Star Wars Insider'' 146|{{InsiderCite|146|Reigniting the Rebellion!}}}} The series begins five years before [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']], fourteen [[Standard year|years]] into the [[Imperial Era|reign]] of the [[Galactic Empire]].{{SW|url=news/nycc-2013-meet-the-inquisitor-the-new-face-of-evil-in-star-wars-rebels|text=NYCC 2013: Meet the Inquisitor, the New Face of Evil in ''Star Wars Rebels''|nobackup=1}}{{Twitter|infinata|status/428247081833070592|[[Pablo Hidalgo]]|nobackup=1}} The general premise is described as follows: "It is a dark time in [[the galaxy]], as the evil Galactic Empire tightens its grip of power from [[Planet|world]] to world. As the series begins, Imperial forces have occupied a [[Lothal|remote planet]], ruling with an iron fist and ruining the lives of its people. But there are a select few who are brave enough to stand up against the endless [[Stormtrooper]]s and [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter|TIE fighters]] of the Empire: the clever and motley crew of the [[starship]] ''[[Ghost]]''. Together, this ragtag group will face threatening new villains, have thrilling adventures, and become heroes."{{SWArchive|url=news/star-wars-rebels-action-figure-packaging-revealed.html|text=''Star Wars Rebels'' Action Figure Packaging Revealed}} ==Development== ===Conception=== {{Quote|They wanted to do an animated show and I loved [Cartoon Network's] Clone Wars and grew up with a lot of animated shows. So we just started to talk about where it would fall in the general Star Wars timeline. Really there was no predetermination going in. It could have been a prequel, sequel, a stand-alone universe.|Simon Kinberg|{{WebCite|url=https://ew.com/article/2014/01/23/star-wars-rebels-interview|text='Star Wars Rebels' interview: New series goes to dark places, embraces 1977 film's spirit|author=Hibberd, James|date=2014-01-23|work=[[Entertainment Weekly Books|''Entertainment Weekly'']]|archivedate=20181201233215}}}} ''Star Wars Rebels'' was created by [[Dave Filoni]], [[Simon Kinberg]], and [[Carrie Beck]]. The concept originated with Beck, who suggested it be about "this [[Wikipedia:The A-Team|A-team]] group that went around righting wrongs." This reminded Filoni of his original concept for ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'',{{WebCite|url=https://collider.com/star-wars-rebels-easter-eggs-episode-7|text=Executive Producer Dave Filoni Talks STAR WARS REBELS, the Game Plan for the Show, Easter Eggs, Advances in Animation, and More|author=Radish, Christina|date=2014-10-04|work=[[Collider (website)|''Collider'']]|archivedate=20200109165831}} which he described in ''[[The Art of Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'': "My rough idea was to deal with a small number of characters [a Jedi Master and Padawan, a smuggler and his girlfriend, and a [[Gungan]] "strongman" called Lunker], have them based on a ''[[Millennium Falcon]]''-style smuggling ship, and involve them in black market trade, war espionage, and other stories that existed outside the giant galactic conflict going on in the background."''[[The Art of Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'' Discussion of where ''Rebels'' would fall in the ''Star Wars'' timeline led to the decision to center the series on the Rebel Alliance. Thus, the series was placed between [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'']] and ''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'', during the reign of the Galactic Empire, though not so close to ''A New Hope'' that it would feel repetitive. In contrast to the galaxy-hopping structure of ''The Clone Wars'', it was decided ''Rebels'' would depict the Rebellion from one group of characters' point of view. According to Filoni, Kinberg likened it to imagining a show set during the [[Wikipedia:American Revolution|American Revolution]] "that was about five guys that were locked up in a farmhouse somewhere fighting against the local British military and without any real knowledge of the larger political movements." He also noted how the [[original trilogy]] mentioned events like the dissolution of the [[Imperial Senate]] without depicting them.{{WebCite|url=https://www.slashfilm.com/star-wars-rebels-interview-dave-filoni|text=/Film Interview: 'Star Wars Rebels' Dave Filoni Answers Burning Questions About The New Series|author=Lussier, Germain|date=2014-08-07|work=[[Wikipedia:/Film|''/Film'']]|archivedate=20190719033559}} The development team set out to differentiate the series from ''The Clone Wars'' by basing much of the visuals on the designs of [[Ralph McQuarrie]]—the artist who developed concept art for much of the original trilogy of films. ''Rebels'' was influenced by ideas developed by [[George Lucas]] for ''[[Star Wars: Underworld]]'',{{WebCite|url=http://www.theforce.net/story/front/SDCC_2014_Complete_Audio_From_Star_Wars_A_New_Dawn_Panel_159102.asp|text=SDCC 2014: Complete Audio From Star Wars: A New Dawn Panel|work=[[TheForce.net]]|archivedate=20190830210911}} and much of the action in ''Rebels'' was influenced by the ''[[Indiana Jones]]'' franchise which George Lucas also contributed to.{{WebCite|url=https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2014/oct/12/star-wars-rebels-disney-dave-filoni|text=Star Wars Rebels: 'A lot of our action is actually inspired by Indiana Jones'|author=Dredge, Stuart|date=2014-10-12|work=[[Wikipedia:The Guardian|''The Guardian'']]|archivedate=20180829072126}} Early in development, Disney wanted a more comedy-oriented series than Lucasfilm was interested in making. Kathleen Kennedy and the ''Rebels'' creative team had to make their case otherwise.{{WebCite|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/lucasfilms-kathleen-kennedy-what-george-846858|text=Lucasfilm's Kathleen Kennedy on What George Lucas Thinks of 'Force Awakens,' Plans for 'Indiana Jones'|author=Masters, Kim|date=2015-12-09|work=[[Wikipedia:The Hollywood Reporter|''The Hollywood Reporter'']]|archivedate=20200622061106}} At one point, Filoni considered involving the [[Death Star plans]] in the show, but abandoned the idea after [[Rogue One: A Star Wars Story|''Rogue One'']] began development.{{WebCite|url=https://comicbook.com/starwars/news/star-wars-rebels-death-star-connection-details-dave-filoni|text=Initial 'Star Wars Rebels' Ideas Involved Discovering Death Star Plans|author=Cavanaugh, Patrick|date=2018-08-07|work=[https://comicbook.com comicbook.com]|archivedate=20200717194954}} He later planned to have appearances from the [[Death Star]] and [[Orson Callan Krennic|Orson Krennic]], but decided it was best to focus on things that directly affect the ''Ghost'' crew.{{WebCite|url=https://www.cinemablend.com/television/2454880/why-star-wars-rebels-didnt-show-the-death-star-in-season-4|text=Why Star Wars Rebels Didn't Show The Death Star In Season 4|author=Hurley, Laura|date=2018-07-31|work=[https://www.cinemablend.com Cinemablend]|archivedate=20190505123507}} ===Production=== {{Quote|It has been great seeing the mind meld between our executive producers Dave Filoni, Simon Kinberg, and Greg Weisman during the writers' conferences. [...] Everyone on the team is so passionate about ''Rebels'', and of course it helps that we are all huge fans of ''Star Wars''!|Athena Portillo, ''Star Wars Insider'' 146|}} [[File:GhostImperialConvoyRaidConcept.jpg|thumb|left|275px|Ralph McQuarrie–inspired concept art of the starship ''Ghost'', chased by TIE fighters.]] [[Lucasfilm]] veteran sculptor [[Darren Marshall]], who worked on ''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' prior to its cancellation, developed sculpts for the core characters of ''Star Wars Rebels'' before leaving Lucasfilm in [[June]] [[2013]].{{SW|url=news/sculpting-the-clone-wars-and-star-wars-rebels-with-darren-marshall|text=Sculpting ''The Clone Wars'' and ''Star Wars Rebels'' with Darren Marshall}} By [[December]] 2013, the production crew had finished developing the series' [[Star Wars Rebels Season One|first season]] and had begun animating the first script.{{InsiderCite|146|Launchpad|Launch Pad}} As of January 2014, the scripts for Season One were halfway completed. Voice-recording had been finished for five episodes, with three more episodes undergoing storyboarding, two more undergoing animation, and the first episode undergoing lighting. Sound design was also underway, with a theme in place for the series.{{InsiderCite|147|Launchpad|Launch Pad}} [[Greg Weisman]] joined the project as an executive producer in [[May]] 2013, though the series had been under development well before then.{{WebCite|url=http://scumandvillainyradio.com|text=Gargoyles, Rain, and Rebels (Episode 14 for 2/28/14)|date=2014-02-28|archivedate=20140302015349|nolive=1}} On [[January 17]], animation supervisor [[Keith Kellogg]] announced that the production crew had wrapped up animation on the first episode of the series.{{Twitter|Keith_Kellogg|statuses/424435812319522816|[[Keith Kellogg]]|archivefile=File:RebelsS01E01AnimationFinish-KelloggTwitter.jpg}} To aid in animating the show, Lucasfilm developed a special tool for [[Wikipedia:Adobe Photoshop|Adobe Photoshop]] that emulates Ralph McQuarrie's artistic style;{{Lucasfilm|url=star-wars-rebels|text=Star Wars Rebels|nolive=1}} the character Zeb Orrelios is based on McQuarie's original concept art for the [[Wookiee]] [[Chewbacca]]. The series' look is also inspired by the work of [[Wikipedia:Hayao Miyazaki|Hayao Miyazaki]]—a favorite of Lucasfilm President [[Kathleen Kennedy]].{{WebCite|url=http://www.latimes.com/entertainment/tv/showtracker/la-et-st-star-wars-rebels-20140310-story.html|text='Star Wars Rebels': Dave Filoni takes 'Star Wars' back to its roots|date=2014-03-11|work=[[Wikipedia:Los Angeles Times|''Los Angeles Times'']]|archivedate=20181019151350}} Filoni requested that the animation crew look at the Disney film [[Wikipedia:Tangled|''Tangled'']], for which 2D facial expressions were created using 3D animation.{{WebCite|url=https://www.ign.com/articles/2014/04/20/wondercon-star-wars-rebels-clip-and-new-details-revealed|text=WonderCon: Star Wars Rebels Clip and New Details Revealed|author=Goldman, Eric|date=2014-04-19|work=[[Wikipedia:IGN|''IGN'']]|archivedate=20200604020933}} Simon Kinberg wrote the series' first two episodes, which serve as a short story arc to introduce the show's main characters. By [[March]] 2014, the entire first season had been mapped out, and according to Greg Weisman, the series as a whole is organized as a three-act play. The first season serves as the first act of the overall series, while the second and third acts may take more than one season. ''Star Wars Rebels'' was overseen by three executive producers: Dave Filoni, Simon Kinberg, and Greg Weisman.{{InsiderCite|143|Launchpad|Launch Pad}} In addition to Filoni, the ''Rebels'' production team included several crew members returning from ''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'': [[Athena Yvette Portillo]] as line producer, [[Kilian Plunkett]] as art director, [[Joel Aron]] as CG effects supervisor, Keith Kellogg as animation supervisor, and [[Steward Lee]] as episodic director. Lee, Filoni's longest-running episodic director from ''The Clone Wars'', was joined in directorial duties by brother [[Steven G. Lee]], a veteran of [[LucasArts]]. [[Kevin Kiner]], who was previously the composer for ''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'', returned as the new music composer for ''Star Wars Rebels''.{{SW|url=news/wondercon-2014-star-wars-rebels-panel-report|text=WonderCon 2014: ''Star Wars Rebels'' Panel Report}} Lucasfilm hired music producer [[Wikipedia:Flux Pavillion|Flux Pavillion]] to remix Kiner's ''Rebels'' main theme.{{WebCite|url=http://www.theforce.net/story/front/Lucasfilm_Commissions_Dubstep_Producer_To_Remix_Star_Wars_Rebels_Theme_160013.asp|text=Lucasfilm Commissions Dubstep Producer To Remix ''Star Wars Rebels'' Theme|author=Geller, Eric|date=2014-09-25|work=[[TheForce.net]]|archivedate=20180829212058}} Other returning crew members from ''The Clone Wars'' included [[Amy Beth Christenson]], [[Andre Kirk]], [[Pat Presley]], and [[Chris Glenn]] on the concept art team, managed by [[Liz Cummings]], as well as [[Paul Zinnes]] on the development team. [[Pablo Hidalgo]], a member of the [[Lucasfilm Story Group]], also worked with the team as a fact-checker. The crew aimed for an overall aesthetic similar to the original trilogy. As such, Joel Aron tried to give the visuals a "grainy look," Matthew Wood used many of the original trilogy's sound effects for the series' soundtrack,{{WebCite|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2014/09/28/arts/television/star-wars-rebels-emulates-the-trilogy-of-old.html|text=Empire Renewed: 'Star Wars Rebels' Emulates the Trilogy of Old|author=Barnes, Brooks|date=2014-09-25|work=[[Wikipedia:The New York Times|''The New York Times'']]|archivedate=20190919135718}} and the crew animated the lightsabers in such a way as to emulate the look of those in the original trilogy.{{WebCite|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/life/tv/2014/10/03/star-wars-rebels-lightsabers-exclusive/16633095|text='Rebels' lightsabers reflect 'Star Wars' roots|author=Truitt, Brian|date=2014-10-03|work=[[Wikipedia:USA Today|''USA Today'']]|archivedate=20191215073958}} ==Release and reception== [[File:Rebelspropaganda.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Imperial propaganda poster created to promote the series]] {{Quote|Citizens of Lothal: It is by Imperial Decree that you are requested to proudly display these posters on behalf of your Empire. As loyal residents of one of the Empire's most vital stations on the Outer Rim, your compliance is appreciated. Imperial Service is a noble endeavor which paves the way for your freedom and security. Remember, it is the will of Emperor Palpatine to ensure the future of a stable and prosperous galaxy.|Letter included in the ''Star Wars Rebels'' propaganda poster mailing promotion|{{Twitter|CanadianFanboy|status/430893963789471744|Andy|nobackup=1}}}} ''Star Wars Rebels'' was first announced on [[March 11]], 2013, as an unnamed animated series set to replace ''Star Wars: The Clone Wars''.{{SW|url=news/a-new-direction-for-lucasfilm-animation|text=A New Direction for Lucasfilm Animation}} Its name and fall 2014 premiere were announced in a press release on [[May 20]], 2013. The first [http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=O1_F7zg4B30 ''Star Wars Rebels'' teaser trailer] debuted on the [https://www.youtube.com/user/starwars ''Star Wars'' YouTube channel] on [[October 7]], 2013.{{SWYouTube|O1_F7zg4B30|Star Wars Rebels Teaser Trailer|sw_url=video/star-wars-rebels-teaser-trailer}} The series' main characters were first revealed at the [[January]] [[2014]] [[Wikipedia:Nuremberg International Toy Fair|Nuremberg International Toy Fair]], which showcased forthcoming ''[[LEGO Star Wars Rebels]]'' sets. The six card backs, when combined together, formed the ''Rebels'' phoenix logo.{{Twitter|RebelsReport|status/431056504523747329|quote=The back of the limited edition set of Rebels propaganda cards make up the #StarWarsRebels Thunderbird logo|Rebels Report|archivedate=20190904233817}} Starting with Chopper, the "grumpy astromech droid" on [[January 28]],{{SW|url=news/star-wars-rebels-meet-chopper-grumpy-astromech-droid|text=Star Wars Rebels: Meet Chopper, Grumpy Astromech Droid}} a series of videos was released that introduced each of the crew members of the ''Ghost''. Kanan was introduced as "the Cowboy Jedi" on [[February 12]], and "the Street-Smart Hero" Ezra Bridger followed on [[February 14]]. Two ''Rebels'' teasers, entitled "Spark" and "Ignite," were released on [[February 17]],{{SWYouTube|1cAwLmyARpE|"Spark" Teaser | Star Wars Rebels|sw_url=video/star-wars-rebels-spark-teaser}}{{SWYouTube|qogqaJ2aXQc|Ignite - Teaser | Star Wars Rebels|sw_url=video/star-wars-rebels-ignite-teaser}} and videos introducing Garazeb Orrelios, "the Muscle," Sabine Wren, "the Explosive Artist," and Hera Syndulla, "the Pilot," were released on [[February 18]], [[February 19|19]], and [[February 20|20]] respectively.
